The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. An action-adventure game developed by Nintendo, released in 2017 for Nintendo Switch and Wii U. Set in the kingdom of Hyrule, you control Link awakening from a century-long slumber to defeat Calamity Ganon and rescue Princess Zelda. Its revolutionary open-world design—freedom to approach objectives in any order—redefined sandbox exploration and proved Nintendo's mastery of environmental storytelling. The core philosophy is to go anywhere and do anything. You can attempt the final boss fight immediately upon leaving the initial tutorial area, or spend hundreds of hours exploring. A durability system on weapons forces you to adapt—nearly every weapon breaks after use, encouraging experimentation rather than reliance on single gear sets. An interactive physics engine allows creative problem-solving. You can climb any surface, use fire to create updrafts, and combine ingredients and items in unexpected ways. Four Divine Beasts serve as dungeons corresponding to elemental powers, and each can be tackled in any order with solutions often emerging from the environment rather than puzzle-lock based. One hundred twenty Shrines scattered across the overworld provide ability upgrades and encourage exploration. Environmental clues replace quest markers—you read the landscape by looking for smoke from monster camps, distant towers, and NPC hints to navigate and discover secrets. Breath of the Wild became a system-seller for Switch and won countless Game of the Year awards, spawning the "Zelda-like" design philosophy of open-world, player-driven gameplay throughout the industry.
